title.zh: 卷七十九上 儒林列傳
title.raw: 卷七十九上 儒林列傳 Volume 79a: Biographies of Confucian Scholars 1

sentences.zh: 昔王莽、更始之際，天下散亂，禮乐分崩，典文残落。

translations.literal: In the time of Wang Mang and of Gengshi, the realm was scattered in disorder; ritual and music collapsed in ruin, and canonical writings survived only in fragments.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wang Mang and the Gengshi court the empire came apart: court ritual fell silent, music was forgotten, and the textual tradition of the classics lay in tatters.

sentences.zh: 及光武中興，爱好經术，未及下車，而先访儒雅，采求阙文，补缀漏逸。

translations.literal: When Guangwu restored the dynasty, he loved the classics and their technical scholarship; before he had even descended from his carriage he first sought out men of cultivated learning, gathered texts that were missing, and patched what had leaked away or been lost.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Guangwu raised the house of Han again, he turned to classical learning with real passion: almost before his chariot wheels had stopped, he was already summoning scholars, hunting down lacunae in the canon, and piecing the tradition back together.

sentences.zh: 先是，四方學士多懷协图書，遁逃林薮。

translations.literal: Before this, scholars from the four quarters for the most part carried annotated charts and books with them and fled into the forests and marshes.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, learned men across the provinces had fled the cities with their annotated manuscripts, taking refuge deep in the hills.

sentences.zh: 自是莫不抱負坟策，云会京师，范升、陳元、鄭興、杜林、卫宏、劉昆、桓荣之徒，继踵而集。

translations.literal: From this time none failed to shoulder bundles of ancient lore; they converged on the capital like clouds—Fan Sheng, Chen Yuan, Zheng Xing, Du Lin, Wei Hong, Liu Kun, Huan Rong, and their like came in succession and assembled.
translations.idiomatic: After that, scholars arrived in Luoyang in waves, their satchels heavy with old texts—Fan Sheng, Chen Yuan, Zheng Xing, Du Lin, Wei Hong, Liu Kun, Huan Rong, and others—until the capital thronged with classicists.

sentences.zh: 于是立《五經》博士，各以家法教授，《易》有施、孟、梁丘、京氏，《尚書》歐陽、大小夏侯，《詩》齊、鲁、韓，《禮》大小戴，《春秋》严、颜、凡十四博士，太常差次总領焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon Erudites for the Five Classics were established; each taught according to his school's transmission—for the Changes there were Shi, Meng, Liangqiu, and the house of Jing; for the Documents, Ouyang and the Greater and Lesser Xiahou; for the Odes, Qi, Lu, and Han; for the Rites, the Greater and Lesser Dai; for the Spring and Autumn, the Yan and Yan Gongyang traditions—in all fourteen Erudites, whom the Grand Chamberlain ranked in order and oversaw in chief.
translations.idiomatic: The court then set up chairs for the Five Classics—fourteen Erudites in all, each line teaching its own school: the Changes in the traditions of Shi, Meng, Liangqiu, and Jing; the Documents with Ouyang and the two Xiahou houses; the Odes in Qi, Lu, and Han; the Rites under the two Dai masters; the Spring and Autumn in the two Gongyang houses associated with the Yan and Yan lineages—with the Grand Chamberlain supervising the whole corps.

sentences.zh: 建武五年，乃修起太學，稽式古典，笾豆干戚之容，备之于列，服方領习矩步者，委它乎其中。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jianwu the Imperial Academy was rebuilt; it took the ancient models as its pattern; the postures of baskets, beans, shield, and axe-heads were fully arrayed in their ranks, and those who wore square collars and practiced measured paces moved at ease within it.
translations.idiomatic: In 29 CE the emperor rebuilt the Imperial Academy on classical lines: ritual vessels and dance regalia stood ranked for instruction, and students in their square-cut collars paced the courtyards with a scholar's deliberate tread.

sentences.zh: 中元元年，初建三雍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongyuan the Three Enclosures were first established.
translations.idiomatic: In 56 CE the court began work on the three ritual precincts—the Bright Hall, the Circular Moat, and the suburban altars.

sentences.zh: 明帝即位，親行其禮。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming ascended the throne, he personally performed these rites.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming, on taking the throne, went in person to celebrate the great state ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 天子始冠通天，衣日月，备法物之驾，盛清道之仪，坐明堂而朝群后，登靈台以望云物，袒割辟雍之上，尊养三老五更。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven for the first time capped himself with the Tongtian headdress, wore robes patterned with sun and moon, prepared the chariot with its full regalia of insignia, and magnified the protocol of clearing the road; he sat in the Bright Hall to hold court over the host of lords, ascended the Spirit Terrace to observe the clouds and prodigies, bared his shoulder and cut the sacrificial meat above the Circular Moat, and with honor supported the Three Elders and the Five Renewed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor now wore the Tongtian crown and the ritual robes emblazoned with sun and moon; his state chariot rolled out with full panoply and an escort that cleared every avenue. From the Bright Hall he received the feudatories, from the Spirit Terrace he read the omens in sky and weather, and at the Circular Moat he offered the joint sacrifice and received the Three Elders and Five Renewed with all due reverence.

sentences.zh: 飨射禮毕，帝正坐自講，諸儒执經問难于前，冠带缙绅之人，圜桥门而觀听者盖億萬计。

translations.literal: When the communal banquet and archery rites were finished, the emperor sat upright and lectured on his own; the various Confucians held the classics and posed difficult questions before him; men in caps, sashes, and silken girdle-pendants who ringed the Bridge Gate to listen were reckoned in the tens of myriads.
translations.idiomatic: After the banquet and archery ritual ended, the emperor took the teacher's seat and expounded the texts himself while classicists pressed him with knotty questions; gentry in court dress packed the approaches to the Academy's Bridge Gate, the crowd said to number in the hundreds of thousands.

sentences.zh: 其后复爲功臣子孫、四姓末属别立校舍，搜选高能以受其業，自期门羽林之士，悉令通《孝經》章句，匈奴亦遣子入學。

translations.literal: After this, dormitories were separately established for the descendants of merit subjects and for junior members of the Four Surnamed clans; men of outstanding ability were sought out and selected to receive instruction in them; from the gentlemen of the Palace Guard and Feathered Forest onward, all were ordered to master the chapter-and-verse glosses of the Classic of Filial Piety, and the Xiongnu also sent sons to enter study.
translations.idiomatic: The court then added halls for the heirs of founding generals and for cadet lines of the great consort houses, enrolling only the brightest pupils; even guardsmen of the Palace Guard and Feathered Forest were required to learn the Classic of Filial Piety by heart, and Xiongnu princes were sent to sit among the students.

sentences.zh: 濟濟乎，洋洋乎，盛于永平矣！

translations.literal: How stately! How vast! It flourished in the Yongping era!
translations.idiomatic: Never was learning so august, never so wide-flung—the Yongping years were the high summer of Han scholarship.

sentences.zh: 初，光武遷還洛陽，其經牒秘書載之二千余两，自此以后，参倍于前。

translations.literal: At first, when Guangwu moved the capital back to Luoyang, the classic tablets and secretariat documents loaded onto more than two thousand carts; from this time onward they were three times as many as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangwu restored Luoyang as the capital, he shipped more than two thousand cartloads of archives and classical texts eastward, and the imperial library soon held three times what it had under the Western Han.

sentences.zh: 及董卓移都之際，吏民扰亂，自辟雍、東觀、兰台、石室、宣明、鸿都諸藏典策文章，竞共剖散，其缣帛图書，大則连爲帷盖，小乃制爲□囊。

translations.literal: When Dong Zhuo shifted the capital, officials and common people were thrown into turmoil; from the Biyong, Eastern Pavilion, Orchid Terrace, Stone Chamber, Xuanyang, and Hongdu repositories, all stored ordinances, policies, and writings were plundered and scattered together; as for the silken books, the large pieces were joined into curtains and canopies, the small were fashioned into pouches and bags.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo's forced removal of the court unleashed chaos: depositories from the Academy to the Hongdu archive were looted wholesale; bolts of silk that had carried the classics were torn up for tent hangings or cut into money purses.

sentences.zh: 及王允所收而西者。

translations.literal: As for those which Wang Yun gathered and sent west.
translations.idiomatic: What Wang Yun managed to salvage and convoy toward Chang'an was another matter.

sentences.zh: 裁七十余乘，道路艰远，复弃其半矣。

translations.literal: They amounted to only a little more than seventy cartloads; the road was hard and distant, and half were abandoned again.
translations.idiomatic: That rescue train came to barely seventy wagons, and the long march west cost half of them along the way.

sentences.zh: 后長安之亂，一時焚荡，莫不泯盡焉。

translations.literal: Later, in the disorders at Chang'an, everything was burned and swept away in a single moment, and none failed to be utterly destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Then came the sack of Chang'an: flames finished what banditry had begun, and almost nothing survived.

sentences.zh: 東京學者猥衆，难以详載，今但录其能通經名家者，以爲《儒林篇》。

translations.literal: The scholars of the Eastern Capital were exceedingly numerous and hard to record in detail; now I shall only set down those able to penetrate the classics and make a name by them, to constitute the 'Forest of Confucians' chapter.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Han produced more classicists than any catalogue could hold; this chapter limits itself to those who mastered a canon and won lasting repute—the 'Forest of Confucians.'

sentences.zh: 其自有列傳者，則不兼書。

translations.literal: Those who already have their own biographies I do not also write here.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone granted a separate biography elsewhere is not repeated in these pages.

sentences.zh: 若师资所承，宜标名爲证者，乃著之云。

translations.literal: If, as for teacher-student succession, it is fitting to mark names as evidence, then I record them thus.
translations.idiomatic: Where a teacher-pupil line needs a name for verification, I note it explicitly.

sentences.zh: 《前書》云：田何傳《易》授丁寬，丁寬授田王孫，王孫授沛人施雠、東海孟喜、琅邪梁丘贺，由是《易》有施、孟、梁丘之學。

translations.literal: The Former Documents states: Tian He transmitted the Changes and handed them on to Ding Kuan; Ding Kuan handed them on to Tian Wangsun; Wangsun handed them on to Shi Chou of Pei, Meng Xi of the Eastern Sea, and Liangqiu He of Langye—whereby for the Changes there were the traditions of Shi, Meng, and Liangqiu.
translations.idiomatic: The Han shu records the old line: Tian He taught Ding Kuan, Ding Kuan taught Tian Wangsun, and Wangsun passed the Changes to Shi Chou, Meng Xi, and Liangqiu He—hence the three orthodox schools of the classic.

sentences.zh: 又東郡京房受《易》于梁國焦延壽，别爲京氏學。

translations.literal: Further, Jing Fang of Dong commandery received the Changes from Jiao Yanshou of Liang state and separately constituted the house of Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang of Dong commandery studied under Jiao Yanshou in Liang and founded a fourth line, the Jing school.

sentences.zh: 又有東莱费直，傳《易》，授琅邪王横，爲费氏學。

translations.literal: There was also Fei Zhi of Donglai, who transmitted the Changes and handed them on to Wang Heng of Langye, constituting the house of Fei.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Zhi of Donglai taught Wang Heng of Langye, and their commentary became the Fei tradition.

sentences.zh: 本以古字，号《古文易》。

translations.literal: Originally because of ancient-character forms, it was styled the 'Changes in ancient script.'
translations.idiomatic: It relied on old-graph forms and was known as the archaic-text Changes.

sentences.zh: 又沛人高相傳《易》，授子康及兰陵毋将永，爲高氏學。

translations.literal: Further, Gao Xiang of Pei transmitted the Changes, handing them on to his son Kang and to Wu Jiang Yong of Lanling, constituting the house of Gao.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xiang of Pei passed the text to his son Gao Kang and to Wu Jiang Yong in Lanling, founding the Gao school.

sentences.zh: 施、孟、梁丘、京氏四家皆立博士，费、高二家未得立。

translations.literal: The four houses of Shi, Meng, Liangqiu, and Jing all had Erudites established; the two houses of Fei and Gao did not obtain establishment.
translations.idiomatic: Court chairs went to Shi, Meng, Liangqiu, and Jing; Fei and Gao never won imperial recognition.

sentences.zh: 劉昆字桓公，陳留東昏人，梁孝王之胤也。

translations.literal: Liu Kun, courtesy name Huanggong, was a man of Donghun in Chenliu, a descendant of Prince Xiao of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun (Huanggong), a native of Donghun in Chenliu, traced his descent from Prince Xiao of Liang.

sentences.zh: 少习容禮。

translations.literal: In youth he practiced deportment rites.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he trained in ritual bearing and formal etiquette.

sentences.zh: 平帝時，受《施氏易》于沛人戴宾。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Ping, he received the Changes in the Shi tradition from Dai Bin of Pei.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ping he studied the Shi Changes with Dai Bin of Pei.

sentences.zh: 能弹雅琴，知清角之操。

translations.literal: He was able to play the refined zither and knew the piece 'Clear Corner.'
translations.idiomatic: He played the qin to a professional standard and had mastered the demanding "Clear Corner" mode.

sentences.zh: 王莽世，教授弟子恒五百余人。

translations.literal: In the age of Wang Mang he instructed disciples, constantly more than five hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wang Mang he kept a private academy of well over five hundred students.

sentences.zh: 每春秋飨射，常备列典仪，以素木瓠叶爲俎豆，桑弧蒿矢，以射“菟首”。

translations.literal: Whenever in spring and autumn there were the communal banquet and archery rites, he always fully arranged the canonical observances, using plain wood and gourd-leaf for the stands and bowls, mulberry bow and artemisia arrows, to shoot at the 'Rabbit's Head' target.
translations.idiomatic: Each spring and autumn he staged the full village archery ritual with scrupulous simplicity—wooden vessels, gourd ladles, mulberry bows, artemisia shafts—aiming at the classic "rabbit" butt.

sentences.zh: 每有行禮，县宰辄率吏属而觀之。

translations.literal: Whenever he performed the rites, the county magistrate always led his clerical staff to observe.
translations.idiomatic: The county magistrate would round up his entire office to watch whenever Kun held ceremony.

sentences.zh: 王莽以昆多聚徒衆，私行大禮，有僭上心，乃系昆及家属于外黄狱。

translations.literal: Wang Mang, because Kun gathered many followers and privately performed great rites with a mind that usurped the ruler's, thereupon bound Kun and his household dependents in the prison of Waihuang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mang decided that a private teacher who drew such crowds and staged state-sized rituals was lèse-majesté; he threw Kun and his family into the Waihuang jail.

sentences.zh: 寻莽敗得免。

translations.literal: Soon Mang was defeated and he obtained release.
translations.idiomatic: He walked free as soon as Wang Mang fell.

sentences.zh: 既而天下大亂，昆避难河南負犊山中。

translations.literal: Subsequently, when the realm was greatly in disorder, Kun fled calamity into the Fudou Mountains in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: When the civil wars began, he took refuge in the Fudou range south of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 建武五年，舉孝廉，不行，遂逃，教授于江陵。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jianwu he was recommended as Filial and Incorrupt but did not take office; he thereupon fled and taught at Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: In 29 CE a nomination as Filial and Incorrupt reached him; he declined, went underground, and reopened his school at Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 光武聞之，即除爲江陵令。

translations.literal: When Guangwu heard of it, he immediately appointed him Jiangling magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangwu, hearing of the recluse-scholar, named him magistrate of Jiangling on the spot.

sentences.zh: 時，县连年火災，昆辄向火叩頭，多能降雨止風。

translations.literal: At that time the county suffered fires year after year; Kun always bowed his head toward the fire and for the most part was able to make rain fall and stop the wind.
translations.idiomatic: Fires raged year after year until Kun, kneeling toward the blaze, prayed rain down and calmed the wind—so the county believed.

sentences.zh: 征拜議郎，稍遷侍中、弘農太守。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Gentleman Consultant, and in time was promoted to Palace Attendant and Administrator of Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: The court recalled him as a Gentleman Consultant, then moved him up to Palace Attendant and governor of Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 先是，崤、黾驿道多虎災，行旅不通。

translations.literal: Before this, on the post-road through Xiao and Meng there were many tiger calamities, and travelers could not pass.
translations.idiomatic: For years the courier road through the Xiao and Meng passes had been a killing ground for tigers, and caravans dared not use it.

sentences.zh: 昆爲政三年，仁化大行，虎皆負子度河。

translations.literal: Kun held office for three years; humane transformation was greatly practiced, and the tigers all carried their cubs across the river.
translations.idiomatic: Within three years of Kun's humane government the tigers were said to have ferried their cubs north across the Yellow River, leaving the district in peace.

sentences.zh: 帝聞而异之。

translations.literal: The emperor heard of it and considered it strange.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard the story and marveled.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，征代杜林爲光禄勋。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was summoned to replace Du Lin as Superintendent of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: In 46 CE he was called to the capital to succeed Du Lin as Superintendent of the Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 詔問昆曰：“前在江陵，反風灭火，后守弘農，虎北度河，行何德政而致是事？

translations.literal: An edict asked Kun, saying: 'Formerly at Jiangling you turned the wind back and extinguished the fire; later as guardian of Hongnong the tigers crossed north over the river—what virtuous government did you practice to bring about these things?'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked him point-blank: "At Jiangling you prayed a head wind around and snuffed a blaze; in Hongnong you cleared the hills of tigers. What magic of good government produced that?"

sentences.zh: ”昆對曰：“偶然耳。

translations.literal: Kun replied, saying: 'It was coincidence, that is all.'
translations.idiomatic: Kun answered simply, "Sheer chance, Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: ”左右皆笑其质讷。

translations.literal: Those on his left and right all laughed at his plain dullness.
translations.idiomatic: The attendants snickered at his wooden honesty.

sentences.zh: 帝叹曰：“此乃長者之言也。

translations.literal: The emperor sighed and said: 'These are indeed the words of an elder.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed. "That is how a gentleman speaks."

sentences.zh: ”顧命書諸策。

translations.literal: He turned his gaze and ordered it written on the various slips.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the reply copied into the court diary.

sentences.zh: 乃令入授皇太子及諸王小侯五十余人。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered him to enter and instruct the heir apparent and the various kings and minor marquises, more than fifty persons.
translations.idiomatic: Kun was then brought in to tutor the crown prince and more than fifty royal sons and young nobles.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，拜骑都尉。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he was appointed Chief Commandant of Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In 51 CE he received the rank of Chief Commandant of Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 三十年，以老乞骸骨，詔賜洛陽第舍，以千石禄終其身。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, on account of old age he begged for his bones; an edict granted him a residence in Luoyang and he ended his life on a salary of one thousand piculs.
translations.idiomatic: In 54 CE he asked to retire; the court gave him a house in Luoyang and a full thousand-picul stipend for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 中元二年卒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhongyuan he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 57 CE.

sentences.zh: 子軼，字君文，傳昆業，门徒亦盛。

translations.literal: His son Yi, courtesy name Junwen, transmitted Kun's enterprise, and his disciples were likewise numerous.
translations.idiomatic: His son Liu Yi (Junwen) inherited the school, and the lecture hall stayed as crowded as ever.

sentences.zh: 永平中，爲太子中庶子。

translations.literal: In the Yongping period he served as Palace Gentleman for Household Affairs to the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongping era he became a senior attendant of the crown prince's household.

sentences.zh: 建初中，稍遷宗正，卒官，遂世掌宗正焉。

translations.literal: In the Jianchu period he was gradually promoted to Director of the Imperial Clan; he died in office, and thereafter the family generation after generation held the Directorship of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Zhang he rose to Director of the Imperial Clan and died in that post; his descendants held the same office for generations.

sentences.zh: 洼丹字子玉，南陽育陽人也。

translations.literal: Wa Dan, courtesy name Ziyu, was a man of Yuyang in Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wa Dan (Ziyu) came from Yuyang in Nanyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 世傳《孟氏易》。

translations.literal: For generations his family transmitted the Changes in the Meng tradition.
translations.idiomatic: His family had taught the Meng commentary on the Changes for generations.

sentences.zh: 王莽時，常避世教授，专志不仕，徒衆数百人。

translations.literal: In the time of Wang Mang he constantly avoided the age and taught, with single-minded resolve not taking office; his followers numbered in the hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wang Mang he withdrew from public life, refused every summons, and kept several hundred private students.

sentences.zh: 建武初，爲博士，稍遷，十一年，爲大鸿胪。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianwu he became an Erudite, was gradually promoted, and in the eleventh year became Grand Herald.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Guangwu's reign he entered the academy as an Erudite, rose step by step, and in 35 CE reached the post of Grand Herald.

sentences.zh: 作《易通論》七篇，世号《洼君通》。

translations.literal: He composed seven chapters of 'Comprehensive Discourse on the Changes,' which the age styled 'Lord Wa's Comprehensive Exposition.'
translations.idiomatic: His seven treatises On the Changes circulated under the nickname "Wa the Generalist."

sentences.zh: 丹學义研深，《易》家宗之，稱爲大儒。

translations.literal: Dan's learning in meaning was researched to depth; the Changes specialists took him as their authority, and he was styled a great Confucian.
translations.idiomatic: Changes scholars deferred to him as the deepest voice of their generation and hailed him as a great master.

sentences.zh: 十七年，卒于官，年七十。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he died in office, aged seventy.
translations.idiomatic: He died in harness in 41 CE, at the age of seventy.

sentences.zh: 時，中山觟陽鸿，字孟孫，亦以《孟氏易》教授，有名稱，永平中爲少府。

translations.literal: At that time Guiyang Hong of Zhongshan, courtesy name Mengsun, likewise taught by the Changes in the Meng tradition, had a reputation and a name, and in the Yongping period became Privy Treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: About the same time Guiyang Hong of Zhongshan (Mengsun) taught the same Meng Changes to wide acclaim and ended up as Privy Treasurer during the Yongping years.

sentences.zh: 任安字定祖，广汉绵竹人也。

translations.literal: Ren An, courtesy name Dingzu, was a man of Mianzhu in Guanghan.
translations.idiomatic: Ren An (Dingzu) was a native of Mianzhu in Guanghan.

sentences.zh: 少游太學，受《孟氏易》，兼通数經。

translations.literal: In youth he studied at the Imperial Academy, received the Changes in the Meng tradition, and was broadly conversant with several classics.
translations.idiomatic: He read the Meng Changes at the Imperial Academy and picked up the other canons besides.

sentences.zh: 又从同郡楊厚學图谶，究極其术。

translations.literal: Further, from Yang Hou of the same commandery he studied charts and prophecies and exhaustively plumbed that art.
translations.idiomatic: He also apprenticed himself to Yang Hou of Guanghan in chart divination and pushed that occult science as far as it would go.

sentences.zh: 時人稱曰：“欲知仲桓問任安。

translations.literal: People of the time said: 'If you wish to know Zhonghuan, ask Ren An.'
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries had a saying: "Need news of Zhonghuan? Ask Ren An."

sentences.zh: ”又曰：“居今行古任定祖。

translations.literal: ' They also said: 'Dwelling in the present yet practicing antiquity—Ren Dingzu.'
translations.idiomatic: Another rhyme ran: "Living in today, walking like the ancients—that is Ren Dingzu."

sentences.zh: ”學終，還家教授，諸生自远而至。

translations.literal: ' When his studies were finished, he returned home and taught, and students came from afar.
translations.idiomatic: When he finished his course of study he went home and opened a school that drew pupils from distant commanderies.

sentences.zh: 初仕州郡。

translations.literal: At first he served in provincial and commandery office.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career on the staff of local government.

sentences.zh: 后太尉再辟，除博士，公車征，皆稱疾不就。

translations.literal: Later the Grand Commandant twice summoned him; he was appointed Erudite; he was summoned by imperial courier coach—each time he pleaded illness and did not take up office.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Commandant called him twice; the court named him Erudite and sent the imperial coach—each time he pleaded sickness and stayed home.

sentences.zh: 州牧劉焉表荐之，時王涂隔塞，詔命竟不至。

translations.literal: Provincial Governor Liu Yan memorialized recommending him; at that time the royal roads were blocked and cut off, and the edict-order in the end did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Liu Yan recommended him for higher office, but the roads were choked by rebellion and the summons never reached him.

sentences.zh: 年七十九，建安七年，卒于家。

translations.literal: At age seventy-nine, in the seventh year of Jian'an, he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home in 202 CE, aged seventy-nine.

sentences.zh: 楊政字子行，京兆人也。

translations.literal: Yang Zheng, courtesy name Zixing, was a man of the capital district.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zheng (Zixing) came from the metropolitan area around Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 少好學，从代郡范升受《梁丘易》，善说經書。

translations.literal: In youth he loved learning; from Fan Sheng of Dai commandery he received the Changes in the Liangqiu tradition, and he was good at expounding the classics.
translations.idiomatic: He studied the Liangqiu Changes under Fan Sheng of Dai and excelled at lively exegesis.

sentences.zh: 京师爲之语曰：“说經铿铿楊子行。

translations.literal: The capital made a saying of him: 'Expounding the classics with a clang—Yang Zixing.'
translations.idiomatic: The capital coined a jingle: "Clang-clang exegesis—that is Yang Zixing."

sentences.zh: ”教授数百人。

translations.literal: ' He taught several hundred persons.
translations.idiomatic: His lecture hall held hundreds.

sentences.zh: 范升尝爲出妇所告，坐系狱，政乃肉袒，以箭贯耳，抱升子潜伏道傍，候車驾，而持章叩頭大言曰：“范升三娶，唯有一子，今适三歲，孤之可哀。

translations.literal: Fan Sheng had once been denounced by a divorced wife and sat bound in prison; Yang Zheng thereupon bared his torso, ran an arrow through his ear, embraced Fan Sheng's son and lay hidden beside the road, waited for the imperial carriage, and holding a petition knocked his head and cried aloud, saying: 'Fan Sheng thrice married and has only one son; he is now just three years old—how pitiable to orphan him.'
translations.idiomatic: When Fan Sheng landed in jail on a complaint from a former wife, Yang stripped to the waist, threaded an arrow through his own earlobe, and hid by the roadside with Fan's toddler in his arms. As the emperor's train approached he thrust forward his memorial and shouted that Fan, thrice married, had but this one three-year-old boy—would the throne orphan him?

sentences.zh: ”武骑虎贲惧惊乘舆，舉弓射之，犹不肯去；

translations.literal: The martial riders and tiger-bodyguards feared startling the imperial conveyance and raised bows to shoot him, yet he still would not depart;
translations.idiomatic: Household guards raised bows, fearing he would spook the imperial horses, but he would not budge;

sentences.zh: 旄頭又以戟叉政，伤胸，政犹不退。

translations.literal: the plumed van-guard also used halberds to stab at Yang Zheng, wounding his breast, yet Yang Zheng still did not withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: plumed halberdiers jabbed him in the chest, yet he still pressed forward.

sentences.zh: 哀泣辞请，有感帝心，詔曰：“乞楊生师。

translations.literal: Weeping in grief he pleaded in his plea, and it moved the emperor's heart; an edict said: 'Grant Master Yang's request concerning the teacher.'
translations.idiomatic: His weeping plea moved the throne, which issued an edict acceding to Master Yang's plea on Fan's behalf.

sentences.zh: ”即尺一出升，政由是显名。

translations.literal: Immediately the foot-measure edict issued and Fan Sheng was released; Yang Zheng thereby became illustriously known.
translations.idiomatic: An express edict freed Fan Sheng at once, and Yang Zheng's name was on every tongue.

sentences.zh: 爲人嗜酒，不拘小節，果敢自矜，然笃于义。

translations.literal: As a man he loved wine, did not bind himself in small points, was bold and decisive and self-assertive, yet was earnest in duty to friends.
translations.idiomatic: He loved wine, scorned petty decorum, and swaggered with a brawler's confidence, yet he was fiercely loyal.

sentences.zh: 時，帝婿梁松、皇后弟陰就，皆慕其聲名，而请与交友。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor's son-in-law Liang Song and the empress's younger brother Yin Jiu both admired his reputation and asked to befriend him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming's son-in-law Liang Song and Empress Ma's brother Yin Jiu courted his friendship for the glamour of his name.

sentences.zh: 政每共言論，常切磋恳至，不爲屈挠。

translations.literal: Whenever Yang Zheng discoursed with them together, he always ground and polished earnestly to the utmost and did not yield or bend for them.
translations.idiomatic: In debate he pressed them hard and never flattered their rank.

sentences.zh: 尝诣楊虚侯馬武，武难見政，稱疾不爲起。

translations.literal: Once he went to visit Marquis of Yangxu Ma Wu; Wu treated it as difficult to see Yang Zheng and pleaded illness, not rising for him.
translations.idiomatic: Once he called on Ma Wu, Marquis of Yangxu, who snubbed him, pleading sickness and refusing to rise.

sentences.zh: 政入户，径升床排武，把臂责之曰：“卿蒙國恩，备位籓辅，不思求贤以报殊宠，而骄天下英俊，此非养身之道也。

translations.literal: Yang Zheng entered the house, went straight up on the couch, pushed Wu aside, grasped his arm and rebuked him, saying: 'You have received the state's grace and fill a place as bulwark assistant; you do not think to seek the worthy to repay extraordinary favor, but instead are arrogant toward the outstanding men of the realm—this is not the way to nurture life.'
translations.idiomatic: Yang walked in, shoved Ma aside on his own couch, seized his arm, and scolded him: "You owe the dynasty everything, yet you sneer at men of talent instead of recruiting them. That is no way to keep body and fortune safe."

sentences.zh: 今日动者刀入胁。

translations.literal: 'If today there is movement, the knife enters the ribs.'
translations.idiomatic: "Stir again and the blade goes between your ribs."

sentences.zh: ”武諸子及左右皆大惊，以爲見劫，操兵满侧，政颜色自若。

translations.literal: Wu's various sons and those on his left and right were all greatly alarmed, thinking they had been seized by bandits; they grasped weapons filling the sides, while Yang Zheng's facial color was as if nothing had happened.
translations.idiomatic: Ma's sons and guards panicked, thinking it a hold-up, and leveled weapons from every side while Yang chatted on as calmly as if he were at a wine party.

sentences.zh: 会陰就至，责数武，令爲交友。

translations.literal: It happened that Yin Jiu arrived, reproved Wu in enumeration, and ordered him to become friends in association.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Jiu walked in, berated Ma Wu, and ordered him to make peace with Yang.

sentences.zh: 其刚果任情，皆如此也。

translations.literal: His being bold, decisive, and following his impulses were all like this.
translations.idiomatic: His rash courage was always of that stamp.

sentences.zh: 建初中，官至左中郎将。

translations.literal: In the Jianchu period he reached office as Left Leader of Court Gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Zhang he rose to Left Leader of Court Gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 張興字君上，颍川鄢陵人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Xing, courtesy name Junshang, was a man of Yanling in Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xing (Junshang) was a native of Yanling in Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 习《梁丘易》以教授。

translations.literal: He studied the Changes in the Liangqiu tradition in order to teach.
translations.idiomatic: He made his career teaching the Liangqiu Changes.

sentences.zh: 建武中，舉孝廉爲郎，谢病去，复歸聚徒。

translations.literal: In the Jianwu period he was recommended as Filial and Incorrupt and became a gentleman; he declined citing illness and left, then returned again to gather disciples.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jianwu years he took a nominal court appointment on a Filial-and-Incorrupt nomination, resigned on grounds of health, and went back to his school.

sentences.zh: 后辟司徒冯勤府，勤舉爲教廉，稍遷博士。

translations.literal: Later he was summoned to the bureau of Minister of Education Feng Qin; Qin recommended him as a recommendee (the chapter text reads 教廉, probably for 孝廉), and he was gradually promoted to Erudite.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Minister of Education Feng Qin later took him on staff and nominated him on the recommendee rolls; he rose to become an Erudite.

sentences.zh: 永平初，遷侍中祭酒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongping he was promoted to Libationer among the Palace Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yongping era he became chief academician among the emperor's Palace Attendants.

sentences.zh: 十年，拜太子少傅。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was appointed Junior Tutor to the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In 67 CE he was named Junior Tutor to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 显宗数访問經术。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong repeatedly visited and inquired into classical scholarship.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming often summoned him to talk about the classics.

sentences.zh: 既而聲稱著聞，弟子自远至者，著录且萬人，爲梁丘家宗。

translations.literal: Thereupon his fame resounded conspicuously; disciples who came from afar, recorded on the rolls, were nearly ten thousand persons, and he became the patriarch of the Liangqiu house.
translations.idiomatic: His reputation spread until nearly ten thousand students had enrolled from every quarter, and he stood as the foremost voice of the Liangqiu school.

sentences.zh: 十四年，卒于官。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office in 71 CE.

sentences.zh: 子鲂，傳興業，位至張掖属國都尉。

translations.literal: His son Fang transmitted Xing's enterprise and reached office as Chief Commandant of the dependent state attached to Zhangye.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhang Fang carried on the school and rose to chief commandant of the Zhangye dependent state.

sentences.zh: 戴憑字次仲，汝南平舆人也。

translations.literal: Dai Ping, courtesy name Cizhong, was a man of Pingyu in Runan.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Ping, Cizhong, came from Pingyu in Runan commandery.

sentences.zh: 习《京氏易》。

translations.literal: He studied the Changes in the Jing tradition.
translations.idiomatic: He trained in the Jing commentary on the Changes.

sentences.zh: 年十六，郡舉明經，征试博士，拜郎中。

translations.literal: At age sixteen the commandery recommended him as Understanding the Classics; he was summoned, examined for Erudite, and appointed Gentleman of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen he won a provincial nomination for classical learning, passed the Erudite examination, and received a Gentleman's appointment.

sentences.zh: 時，詔公卿大会，群臣皆就席，憑独立。

translations.literal: At that time an edict summoned the dukes and high ministers to a great assembly; the host of ministers all took their mats, but Ping alone stood.
translations.idiomatic: When the court convened the high ministers for a great audience, every official took his seat except Dai Ping, who remained standing.

sentences.zh: 光武問其意。

translations.literal: Guangwu asked his intention.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangwu asked why.

sentences.zh: 憑對曰：“博士说經皆不如臣，而坐居臣上，是以不得就席。

translations.literal: Ping replied, saying: 'The Erudites in expounding the classics are all not as good as your servant, yet they sit placed above your servant; therefore I could not take a mat.'
translations.idiomatic: Dai Ping said, "The doctoral scholars cannot match me in exegesis, yet they rank above me—that is why I refuse to sit."

sentences.zh: ”帝即召上殿，令与諸儒难说，憑多所解释。

translations.literal: ' The emperor thereupon summoned him up to the hall, ordered him to engage in difficult disputation with the various Confucians, and Ping for the most part explained much.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had him brought to the dais to debate the other classicists, and Dai carried most of the points.

sentences.zh: 帝善之，拜爲侍中，数进見問得失。

translations.literal: The emperor approved of him, appointed him Palace Attendant, and repeatedly advanced him to audience to ask about gains and losses.
translations.idiomatic: Pleased with his performance, the emperor named him Palace Attendant and often called him in to discuss policy.

sentences.zh: 帝謂憑曰：“侍中当匡补國政，勿有隐情。

translations.literal: The emperor said to Ping: 'A Palace Attendant ought to rectify and supplement state governance; do not harbor hidden feelings.'
translations.idiomatic: He told Dai, "A Palace Attendant is supposed to shore up the government—hold nothing back."

sentences.zh: ”憑對曰：“陛下严。

translations.literal: ' Ping replied, saying: 'Your Majesty is severe.'
translations.idiomatic: Dai answered, "Your Majesty's rule is harsh."

sentences.zh: ”帝曰：“朕何用严？

translations.literal: ' The emperor said: 'With what do I use severity?'
translations.idiomatic: "In what way am I harsh?"

sentences.zh: ”憑曰：“伏見前太尉西曹掾蒋遵，清亮忠孝，學通古今，陛下纳肤受之诉，遂致禁锢，世以是爲严。

translations.literal: ' Ping said: 'I have seen that Jiang Zun, formerly Western Bureau clerk to the Grand Commandant, was pure, bright, loyal, and filial, and his learning penetrated antiquity and the present; Your Majesty accepted skin-deep accusations, thereupon causing him to be bound in prohibition, and the age for this reason considers Your Majesty severe.'
translations.idiomatic: Dai said, "Jiang Zun, who served on the Grand Commandant's staff, was loyal, learned, and upright; Your Majesty listened to shallow slander and threw him in prison. The world calls that severity."

sentences.zh: ”帝怒曰：“汝南子欲复党乎？

translations.literal: ' The emperor angrily said: 'Do you Runan fellows wish to form factions again?'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor snapped, "Are you Runan men trying to form another clique?"

sentences.zh: ”憑出，自系廷尉，有詔敕出。

translations.literal: ' Ping went out, bound himself to the Commandant of Justice, and there was an edict ordering his release.
translations.idiomatic: Dai walked out and surrendered himself to the prison bureau until an edict ordered him freed.

sentences.zh: 后复引見，憑谢曰：“臣无謇谔之節，而有狂瞽之言，不能以尸伏谏，偷生苟活，诚惭聖朝。

translations.literal: ' Later he was again led to audience, and Ping apologized, saying: 'Your servant lacks the integrity of blunt remonstrance, yet had mad and blind words; I was not able to lie as a corpse remonstrating, but stole life and lived ignobly—I am truly ashamed before the sage court.'
translations.idiomatic: When summoned again he apologized: "I lack the courage of a straight remonstrator; I spoke rashly and failed to lay down my life in protest—I am ashamed before the throne."

sentences.zh: ”帝即敕尚書解遵禁锢，拜憑虎贲中郎将，以侍中兼領之。

translations.literal: ' The emperor thereupon ordered the Masters of Writing to release Jiang Zun from prohibition, appointed Ping Colonel of the Grooms of the Yellow Gates, and had him concurrently hold it as Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor at once ordered Jiang Zun released, made Dai Ping a colonel of the imperial guard, and let him keep his Palace Attendant duties as well.

sentences.zh: 正旦朝贺，百僚毕会，帝令群臣能说經者更相难诘，义有不通，辄夺其席以益通者，憑遂重坐五十余席。

translations.literal: On New Year's Day court congratulations, when the hundred officials had all assembled, the emperor ordered the host of ministers who could expound the classics mutually to pose difficult questions; when the meaning was not penetrated, he always stripped away that man's mat to add to the one who penetrated it, and Ping in the end piled up more than fifty mats.
translations.idiomatic: At the New Year's audience the emperor set the classicists to debating one another, stripping a mat from anyone who lost a point and giving it to the victor; Dai Ping ended up sitting on a stack of more than fifty.

sentences.zh: 故京师爲之语曰：“解經不穷戴侍中。

translations.literal: Therefore the capital made a saying of him: 'In unraveling the classics there is no exhausting Palace Attendant Dai.'
translations.idiomatic: The capital rhyme ran: "Ask Dai the Palace Attendant—his exegesis never runs dry."

sentences.zh: ”在职十八年，卒于官，詔賜東园梓器，钱二十萬。

translations.literal: ' He held office eighteen years, died in office, and an edict granted him Eastern Park catalpa coffin-ware and two hundred thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: He served eighteen years and died in post; the court supplied a state coffin from the imperial workshop and two hundred thousand cash toward the funeral.

sentences.zh: 時南陽魏满字叔牙，亦习《京氏易》，教授。

translations.literal: At that time Wei Man of Nanyang, courtesy name Shuya, likewise studied the Changes in the Jing tradition and taught.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Man of Nanyang, known as Shuya, also taught the Jing Changes.

sentences.zh: 永平中，至弘農太守。

translations.literal: In the Yongping period he reached office as Administrator of Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongping era he rose to governor of Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 孫期字仲彧，濟陰成武人也。

translations.literal: Sun Qi, courtesy name Zhongyu, was a man of Chengwu in Jiyin.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Qi, Zhongyu, was from Chengwu in Jiyin commandery.

sentences.zh: 少爲諸生，习《京氏易》、《古文尚書》。

translations.literal: In youth he was a student and studied the Changes in the Jing tradition and the Documents in ancient script.
translations.idiomatic: As a young scholar he mastered the Jing Changes and the archaic-text Documents.

sentences.zh: 家贫，事母至孝，牧豕于大澤中，以奉养焉。

translations.literal: His family was poor; in serving his mother he was supremely filial; he herded pigs in a great marsh in order thereby to support and nourish her.
translations.idiomatic: Poor but devoted to his mother, he kept a herd of pigs in the marshlands to pay for her care.

sentences.zh: 远人从其學者，皆执經壟畔以追之，里落化其仁讓。

translations.literal: Those from afar who followed him in study all grasped the classics along the field ridges to pursue him, and hamlets and villages were transformed by his benevolence and yielding.
translations.idiomatic: Students from distant places trailed him along the furrows with their scrolls open, and the whole countryside took its tone from his gentleness and courtesy.

sentences.zh: 黄巾贼起，過期里陌，相約不犯孫先生舍。

translations.literal: When the Yellow Turban bandits arose, passing through Qi's lanes and paths, they mutually agreed not to violate Master Sun's dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yellow Turbans swept through the district, they pledged among themselves to spare Master Sun's home.

sentences.zh: 郡舉方正，遣吏赍羊、酒请期，期驱豕入草不顧。

translations.literal: The commandery recommended him as Upright and Square; it dispatched a clerk bearing sheep and wine to invite Qi, but Qi drove the pigs into the grass and did not look back.
translations.idiomatic: Nominated as a candidate of unimpeachable character, he was offered sheep and wine by the county clerk; he only drove his pigs deeper into the reeds and ignored the summons.

sentences.zh: 司徒黄琬特辟，不行，終于家。

translations.literal: Minister of Education Huang Wan specially summoned him; he did not go, and ended his life at home.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Minister of Education Huang Wan called for him by special appointment, but he never took office and died at home.

sentences.zh: 建武中，范升傳《孟氏易》，以授楊政，而陳元、鄭衆皆傳《费氏易》，其后馬融亦爲其傳。

translations.literal: In the Jianwu period Fan Sheng transmitted the Changes in the Meng tradition and thereby handed them on to Yang Zheng, while Chen Yuan and Zheng Zhong both transmitted the Changes in the Fei tradition; later Ma Rong also became a transmitter of it.
translations.idiomatic: Under Guangwu, Fan Sheng passed the Meng Changes to Yang Zheng, while Chen Yuan and Zheng Zhong taught the Fei line that Ma Rong later championed.

sentences.zh: 融授鄭玄，玄作《易注》，荀爽又作《易傳》，自是《费氏》興，而《京氏》遂衰。

translations.literal: Rong handed them on to Zheng Xuan; Xuan composed a 'Commentary on the Changes,' and Xun Shuang also composed a 'Tradition on the Changes'; from this time the Fei tradition rose, while the Jing tradition thereupon declined.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Rong taught Zheng Xuan, who wrote a commentary, and Xun Shuang added a subcommentary; the Fei school eclipsed the Jing house.

sentences.zh: 《前書》云：濟南伏生傳《尚書》，授濟南張生及千乘歐陽生，歐陽生授同郡B6 F9寬，寬授歐陽生之子，世世相傳，至曾孫歐陽高，爲《尚書》歐陽氏學；

translations.literal: The Former Documents states: Fu Sheng of Jinan transmitted the Documents, handing them on to Zhang Sheng of Jinan and to Ouyang Sheng of Qiancheng; Ouyang Sheng handed them on to Ni Kuan of the same commandery, Kuan handed them on to Ouyang Sheng's son, generation after generation transmitting, down to great-grandson Ouyang Gao, constituting the Ouyang tradition of the Documents;
translations.idiomatic: The Han shu traces the Documents from Fu Sheng of Jinan to Zhang Sheng and Ouyang Sheng of Qiancheng; Ouyang's pupil Ni Kuan of Jinan passed the text to Ouyang's son, and eight generations later Ouyang Gao headed what became the Ouyang school of the Documents.

sentences.zh: 張生授夏侯都尉，都尉授族子始昌，始昌傳族子胜，爲大夏侯氏學；

translations.literal: Zhang Sheng handed them on to Xiahou Commandant, Commandant handed them on to his agnate nephew Shichang, Shichang transmitted to agnate nephew Sheng, constituting the Greater Xiahou tradition of the Documents;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Sheng's line ran to Xiahou the commandant, then to Xiahou Shichang and Xiahou Sheng—the Greater Xiahou commentary.

sentences.zh: 胜傳从兄子建，建别爲小夏侯氏學：三家皆立博士。

translations.literal: Sheng transmitted to his elder cousin's son Jian, and Jian separately constituted the Lesser Xiahou tradition of the Documents: all three houses had Erudites established.
translations.idiomatic: Xiahou Sheng taught his cousin's son Jian, who founded the Lesser Xiahou variant; all three lines received chairs at court.

sentences.zh: 又鲁人孔安國傳《古文尚書》授都尉朝，朝授胶東庸谭，爲《尚書》古文學，未得立。

translations.literal: Further, Kong Anguo of Lu transmitted the Documents in ancient script and handed them on to Chao, who held the rank of commandant; Chao handed them on to Yong Tan of Jiaodong, constituting the ancient-script learning of the Documents, which did not obtain establishment.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Anguo's archaic-text Documents passed to Commandant Chao and then to Yong Tan of Jiaodong—a line that never won a doctoral chair.

sentences.zh: 歐陽歙

translations.literal: Ouyang Xi
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Xi

sentences.zh: 歐陽歙字正思，乐安千乘人也。

translations.literal: Ouyang Xi, courtesy name Zhengsi, was a man of Qiancheng in Le'an.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Xi, Zhengsi, came from Qiancheng in Le'an.

sentences.zh: 自歐陽生傳《伏生尚書》，至歙八世，皆爲博士。

translations.literal: From Ouyang Sheng's transmission of Fu Sheng's Documents down to Xi was eight generations, and all were Erudites.
translations.idiomatic: Eight generations of his family had held the Ouyang Documents chair without a break.

sentences.zh: 歙既傳業，而恭谦好禮讓。

translations.literal: Xi, having transmitted the enterprise, was moreover respectful, modest, and fond of ritual yielding.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the tradition and wore it lightly—deferential, courteous, quick to yield.

sentences.zh: 王莽時，爲長社宰。

translations.literal: In the time of Wang Mang he was magistrate of Changshe.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wang Mang he served as magistrate of Changshe.

sentences.zh: 更始立，爲原武令。

translations.literal: When Gengshi was established, he became magistrate of Yuanwu.
translations.idiomatic: The Gengshi regime named him magistrate of Yuanwu.

sentences.zh: 世祖平河北，到原武，見歙在县修政，遷河南都尉，后行太守事。

translations.literal: Shizu pacified Hebei; arriving at Yuanwu, he saw that Xi in the county cultivated governance, promoted him to Chief Commandant of Henan, and later had him act in the Administrator's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Guangwu pacified the north and passed through Yuanwu, he was so impressed by Xi's administration that he promoted him to chief commandant of Henan and then acting governor.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，始爲河南尹，封被陽侯。

translations.literal: When Shizu ascended the throne, he first became Intendant of Henan and was enfeoffed as marquis of Beiyang.
translations.idiomatic: After the accession he became intendant of Henan and received the marquisate of Beiyang.

sentences.zh: 建武五年，坐事免官。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jianwu, on account of an affair he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: In 29 CE he lost his post over an unspecified offense.

sentences.zh: 明年，拜楊州牧，遷汝南太守。

translations.literal: The next year he was appointed Governor of Yang province, then promoted to Administrator of Runan.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was named governor of Yang province, then transferred to Runan as administrator.

sentences.zh: 推用贤俊，政稱异迹。

translations.literal: He promoted and employed worthy and outstanding men; his governance was praised as marked by extraordinary traces.
translations.idiomatic: He lifted able men into office, and his administration was counted among the most distinguished of the day.

sentences.zh: 九年，更封夜侯。

translations.literal: In the ninth year his fief was changed and he was enfeoffed as marquis of Ye.
translations.idiomatic: In 33 CE his title was moved to the marquisate of Ye.

sentences.zh: 歙在郡，教授数百人，視事九歲，征爲大司徒。

translations.literal: While Xi was in the commandery he taught several hundred persons; holding office nine years, he was summoned to be Grand Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: In Runan he taught hundreds of students; after nine years in office the court summoned him to be grand minister of education.

sentences.zh: 坐在汝南臧罪千余萬发觉下狱。

translations.literal: He sat in guilt for embezzlement (zang) in Runan of more than ten million cash, which was discovered, and he was cast into prison.
translations.idiomatic: He was jailed when an investigation uncovered more than ten million in corrupt gains from his years in Runan.

sentences.zh: 諸生守阙爲歙求哀者千余人，至有自髡剔者。

translations.literal: Students who guarded the palace gate to seek pity for Xi were more than a thousand persons, to the point that some shaved their heads or mutilated their flesh.
translations.idiomatic: More than a thousand of his students camped at the palace gate to plead for his life; some shaved their heads or cut their flesh in protest.

sentences.zh: 平原禮震，年十七，聞狱当断，驰之京师，行到河内获嘉县，自系，上書求代歙死。

translations.literal: Li Zhen of Pingyuan, aged seventeen, hearing that the prison case was about to be decided, galloped to the capital; proceeding as far as Huojia county in Henei, he bound himself and submitted a memorial begging to die in Xi's stead.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhen, a seventeen-year-old from Pingyuan, raced toward Luoyang when he heard the sentence was near, chained himself at Huojia in Henei, and offered his life for his teacher.

sentences.zh: 曰：“伏見臣师大司徒歐陽歙，學爲儒宗，八世博士，而以臧咎当伏重辜。

translations.literal: He said: 'I have seen that my teacher the Grand Minister of Education Ouyang Xi, whose learning is patriarch among Confucians and who for eight generations has been Erudite, yet on account of embezzlement guilt ought to suffer heavy punishment.'
translations.idiomatic: He wrote: "My teacher Ouyang Xi, grand minister of education, head of the Ru for eight generations of doctoral chairs, now faces execution for a fiscal crime."

sentences.zh: 歙门单子幼，未能傳學，身死之后，永爲廢絕，上令陛下获殺贤之讥，下使學者丧师资之益。

translations.literal: Xi's gate is thin, his son young, not yet able to transmit learning; after his body dies it will forever be cut off and extinguished—above it will cause Your Majesty to incur the ridicule of killing the worthy, below it will cause students to lose the benefit of teacher and model.
translations.idiomatic: His household is small and his heir too young to carry on the school; if he dies the line ends, the throne earns the name of killer of sages, and students lose their master.

sentences.zh: 乞殺臣身以代歙命。

translations.literal: I beg to kill my person in order to substitute for Xi's life.'
translations.idiomatic: I beg you to take my life instead of his."

sentences.zh: ”書奏，而歙已死狱中。

translations.literal: ' When the memorial was submitted, Xi had already died in prison.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial reached the throne only after Ouyang Xi had died in his cell.

sentences.zh: 歙掾陳元上書追訟之，言甚切至，帝乃賜棺木，赠印绶，赙缣三千匹。

translations.literal: Xi's clerk Chen Yuan submitted a memorial afterward suing on his behalf; the words were extremely cutting and thorough, and the emperor thereupon granted a coffin, presented seals and ribbons, and gave three thousand bolts of silk for funeral expenses.
translations.idiomatic: His aide Chen Yuan filed a blistering posthumous appeal; the emperor relented enough to send a coffin, posthumous insignia, and three thousand rolls of silk toward the burial.

sentences.zh: 子复嗣。

translations.literal: His son Fu inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ouyang Fu inherited the marquisate.

sentences.zh: 复卒，无子，國除。

translations.literal: When Fu died, there was no son, and the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu died without an heir, the fief lapsed.

sentences.zh: 濟陰曹曾字伯山，从歙受《尚書》，门徒三千人，位至谏議大夫。

translations.literal: Cao Zeng of Jiyin, courtesy name Boshan, received the Documents from Xi; his disciples were three thousand persons, and he reached office as Grandee Remonstrant and Consultant.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Zeng of Jiyin studied the Documents under Xi, drew three thousand students, and rose to grandee remonstrant.

sentences.zh: 子祉，河南尹，傳父業教授。

translations.literal: His son Zhi, Intendant of Henan, transmitted the father's enterprise and taught.
translations.idiomatic: His son Cao Zhi became intendant of Henan and continued the family school.

sentences.zh: 留陳弇，字叔明，亦受《歐陽尚書》于司徒丁鸿，仕爲蕲長。

translations.literal: Chen Yan of Liu, courtesy name Shuming, likewise received the Ouyang Documents from Grand Minister of Education Ding Hong, and served in office as chief of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yan of Liu, called Shuming, also studied the Ouyang Documents under Ding Hong and served as magistrate of Qi.

sentences.zh: 牟長字君高，乐安臨濟人也。

translations.literal: Mou Chang, courtesy name Jungao, was a man of Linji in Le'an.
translations.idiomatic: Mou Chang, Jungao, hailed from Linji in Le'an.

sentences.zh: 其先封牟，春秋之末，國灭，因氏焉。

translations.literal: His ancestors were enfeoffed at Mou; at the end of the Spring and Autumn period the state was extinguished, and they took it as surname.
translations.idiomatic: The clan took its name from the lost state of Mou, extinguished at the close of the Spring and Autumn era.

sentences.zh: 長少习《歐陽尚書》，不仕王莽世。

translations.literal: Chang in youth studied the Ouyang Documents and did not take office in the age of Wang Mang.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered the Ouyang Documents in youth and refused office under Wang Mang.

sentences.zh: 建武二年，大司空弘特辟，拜博士，稍遷河内太守，坐垦田不實免。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianwu, Grand Minister of Works Hong specially summoned him; he was appointed Erudite, was gradually promoted to Administrator of Henei, and on account of unreality in reported reclaimed fields was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: In 26 CE Grand Minister of Works Zhu Hong gave him a special summons; he became an Erudite, then governor of Henei, until padded land figures cost him his post.

sentences.zh: 長自爲博士及在河内，諸生講學者常有千余人，著录前后萬人。

translations.literal: From the time Chang was an Erudite and while in Henei, students who lectured and studied were constantly more than a thousand persons; those recorded on rolls before and after were ten thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: As Erudite and as governor of Henei he seldom addressed fewer than a thousand auditors; his enrollment rolls ran to ten thousand names over the years.

sentences.zh: 著《尚書章句》，皆本之歐陽氏，俗号爲《牟氏章句》。

translations.literal: He composed 'Chapter-and-Verse Glosses on the Documents,' all based on the Ouyang house; vulgar usage styled them 'Mou's Chapter-and-Verse Glosses.'
translations.idiomatic: His chapter-and-verse gloss on the Documents followed Ouyang throughout and circulated as the Mou commentary.

sentences.zh: 复征爲中散大夫，賜告一歲，卒于家。

translations.literal: He was again summoned as Counsellor of the Palace, was granted leave for one year, and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled as counsellor of the palace, he was granted a year's sick leave and died at home.

sentences.zh: 子纡，又以隐居教授，门生千人。

translations.literal: His son Yu, again by living in reclusion taught, and his disciples were a thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: His son Mou Yu taught from seclusion and kept a thousand disciples.

sentences.zh: 肃宗聞而征之，欲以爲博士，道物故。

translations.literal: Suzong heard of him and summoned him, wishing to make him Erudite, but on the road he died.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhang summoned him for an Erudite chair, but he died en route.

sentences.zh: 宋登字叔陽，京兆長安人也。

translations.literal: Song Deng, courtesy name Shuyang, was a man of Chang'an in the capital district.
translations.idiomatic: Song Deng, Shuyang, was a Chang'an man of the metropolitan area.

sentences.zh: 父由，爲太尉。

translations.literal: His father You was Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: His father Song You had served as grand commandant.

sentences.zh: 登少傳《歐陽尚書》，教授数千人。

translations.literal: Deng in youth transmitted the Ouyang Documents and taught several thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he taught the Ouyang Documents to thousands.

sentences.zh: 爲汝陰令，政爲明能，号稱“神父”。

translations.literal: As magistrate of Ruyin his governance was enlightened and capable, and he was styled 'divine father.'
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Ruyin he governed so well that people called him the divine father.

sentences.zh: 遷趙相，入爲尚書仆射。

translations.literal: He was promoted to chancellor of Zhao, entered service as Deputy Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to chancellor of Zhao, then to deputy director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 顺帝以登明識禮乐，使持節臨太學，奏定曲律，轉拜侍中。

translations.literal: Emperor Shun, because Deng clearly understood ritual and music, sent him bearing credentials to attend the Imperial Academy, memorialized to fix melodies and statutes, and transferred him to appointment as Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shun, valuing his expertise in ritual music, sent him to the Imperial Academy with imperial credentials to settle pitch standards, then promoted him to Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 数上封事，抑退权臣，由是出爲颖川太守。

translations.literal: He repeatedly submitted sealed memorials, restraining and pushing back powerful ministers; for this reason he went out to become Administrator of Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: His sealed memorials checked powerful ministers at court, and he was eased out as governor of Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 市无二價，道不拾遺。

translations.literal: In the market there were not two prices; on the roads nothing picked up was kept.
translations.idiomatic: Under his rule the markets showed a single fair price and lost goods were returned untouched.

sentences.zh: 病免，卒于家，汝陰人配社祠之。

translations.literal: He was dismissed on account of illness, died at home, and the people of Ruyin paired him in sacrifice at the earth altar and sacrificed to him.
translations.idiomatic: Illness forced his retirement; he died at home, and the people of Ruyin enshrined him beside the soil god.

sentences.zh: 張驯字子鯭，濟陰定陶人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Xun, courtesy name Ziru, was a man of Dingtao in Jiyin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xun, Ziru, was from Dingtao in Jiyin.

sentences.zh: 少游太學，能誦《春秋左氏傳》。

translations.literal: In youth he studied at the Imperial Academy and was able to recite the Zuo Tradition of the Spring and Autumn.
translations.idiomatic: At the Imperial Academy he memorized the entire Zuo commentary on the Spring and Autumn.

sentences.zh: 以《大夏侯尚書》教授。

translations.literal: By the Greater Xiahou Documents he taught.
translations.idiomatic: He taught the Greater Xiahou recension of the Documents.

sentences.zh: 辟公府，舉高第，拜議郎。

translations.literal: He was summoned to the Excellencies' offices, recommended in high rank, and appointed Gentleman Consultant.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to the top bureaucracy and graded at the head of his class, he became a gentleman consultant.

sentences.zh: 与蔡邕共奏定《六經》文字。

translations.literal: Together with Cai Yong he jointly memorialized to fix the graphs of the Six Classics.
translations.idiomatic: With Cai Yong he helped fix the official text of the Six Classics on the stone tablets.

sentences.zh: 擢拜侍中，典領秘書近署，甚見纳异。

translations.literal: He was promoted and appointed Palace Attendant, in charge of overseeing the secretariat's near offices, and was greatly received and treated as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Palace Attendant, he supervised the palace library and became a favorite at court.

sentences.zh: 多因便宜陳政得失，朝廷嘉之。

translations.literal: For the most part by opportune convenience he set forth governance's gains and losses, and the court praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He often seized the moment to speak frankly on policy, and the court welcomed it.

sentences.zh: 遷丹陽太守，化有惠政。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Administrator of Danyang; in transformation he had benevolent governance.
translations.idiomatic: As governor of Danyang he earned a reputation for humane rule.

sentences.zh: 光和七年，征拜尚書，遷大司農。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Guanghe he was summoned and appointed Master of Writing, then promoted to Grand Minister of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: In 184 CE he was recalled as a master of writing and promoted to grand minister of agriculture.

sentences.zh: 初平中，卒于官。

translations.literal: In the Chuping period he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office during the Chuping era.

sentences.zh: 尹敏字幼季，南陽堵陽人也。

translations.literal: Yin Min, courtesy name Youji, was a man of Duyang in Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Min, Youji, came from Duyang in Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 少爲諸生。

translations.literal: In youth he was a student.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a student at the provincial academy.

sentences.zh: 初习《歐陽尚書》，后受《古文》，兼善《毛詩》、《穀梁》、《左氏春秋》。

translations.literal: At first he studied the Ouyang Documents; afterward he received the ancient script, and was concurrently good at the Mao Odes, the Guliang, and the Zuo Tradition of the Spring and Autumn.
translations.idiomatic: He started with the Ouyang Documents, added the archaic text, and mastered the Mao Odes, Guliang, and Zuo commentary on the Spring and Autumn.

sentences.zh: 建武二年，上疏陳《洪范》消災之术。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianwu he submitted a memorial setting forth the techniques of the 'Great Plan' for dispelling calamities.
translations.idiomatic: In 26 CE he memorialized on how the "Great Plan" chapter might be used to avert disaster.

sentences.zh: 時，世祖方草创天下，未遑其事，命敏待詔公車，拜郎中，辟大司空府。

translations.literal: At that time Shizu was just beginning to establish the realm and had not leisure for this matter; he ordered Min to await edicts at the imperial coach, appointed him Gentleman of the Palace, and summoned him to the Grand Minister of Works' office.
translations.idiomatic: Guangwu was still fighting for the empire and set the proposal aside, but he put Yin on waiting status at the coach office, named him a gentleman, and later added him to the grand minister of works' staff.

sentences.zh: 帝以敏博通經記，令校图谶，使蠲去崔发所爲王莽著录次比。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Min broadly penetrated the classics and records, ordered him to collate charts and prophecies, and had him eliminate what Cui Fa had done for Wang Mang in compiling and ordering entries.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, knowing Yin's breadth of learning, put him to editing the prophetic corpus and purging the entries Cui Fa had arranged for Wang Mang.

sentences.zh: 敏對曰：“谶書非聖人所作，其中多近鄙别字，颇类世俗之辞，恐疑误后生。

translations.literal: Min replied, saying: 'Prophetic books are not what the sages made; within them are many near-vulgar variant graphs, quite resembling vulgar commoner's phrases—I fear they will mislead later students.'
translations.idiomatic: Yin replied that the apocrypha were not the work of sages, that they bristled with vulgar characters and folk phrasing, and that they would mislead the young.

sentences.zh: ”帝不纳。

translations.literal: ' The emperor did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor brushed the warning aside.

sentences.zh: 敏因其阙文增之曰：“君无口，爲汉辅。

translations.literal: Min, exploiting its missing text, added to it, saying: 'The lord has no mouth; he is helper to Han.'
translations.idiomatic: Yin filled a lacuna in the text with a forged line: "The lord without a mouth shall be helper to Han."

sentences.zh: ”帝見而怪之，召敏問其故。

translations.literal: ' The emperor saw it and considered it strange; he summoned Min and asked the reason.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor noticed the tampering, he called Yin Min in and demanded an explanation.

sentences.zh: 敏對曰：“臣見前人增損图書，敢不自量，窃幸萬一。

translations.literal: Min replied, saying: 'Your servant saw that former men added to and subtracted from chart-books; I dared not measure myself, but privately hoped for one chance in ten thousand.'
translations.idiomatic: Yin answered, "I saw earlier editors alter the prophetic texts and hoped, foolishly, that I might luck into the same favor."

sentences.zh: ”帝深非之，雖竟不罪，而亦以此沈滞。

translations.literal: ' The emperor deeply condemned him; although in the end he was not punished, for this reason he also sank into stagnation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked him harshly; though no formal sentence followed, Yin's career never recovered.

sentences.zh: 与班彪親善，每相遇，辄日旰忘食，夜分不寝，自以爲钟期、伯牙，庄周、惠施之相得也。

translations.literal: He was intimate friends with Ban Biao; whenever they met, they always forgot food though the sun had set, and at midnight split did not sleep, deeming themselves like Zhong Qi and Boya, or Zhuang Zhou and Huishi in mutual understanding.
translations.idiomatic: He and Ban Biao were close as brothers: a single conversation could keep them talking past supper and far into the night, each sure he had found his Zhuangzi to the other's Huizi.

sentences.zh: 后三遷長陵令。

translations.literal: Later, after three promotions, he became magistrate of Changling.
translations.idiomatic: Three promotions later he was magistrate of Changling.

sentences.zh: 永平五年，詔書捕男子周虑。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yongping an edict ordered the arrest of the man Zhou Lü.
translations.idiomatic: In 62 CE an imperial warrant went out for one Zhou Lü.

sentences.zh: 虑素有名稱，而善于敏，敏坐系免官。

translations.literal: Lü had always had a good reputation and was on good terms with Min; Min sat bound and was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Lü was a man of reputation and a friend of Yin Min; the connection landed Yin in jail and cost him his post.

sentences.zh: 及出，叹曰：“喑聾之徒，真世之有道者也。

translations.literal: When he came out, he sighed, saying: 'The mute and deaf sort are truly the men who have the Way in the world.'
translations.idiomatic: On his release he sighed that the truly wise were the deaf who heard nothing of politics.

sentences.zh: 何謂察察而遇斯患乎？

translations.literal: What is called being perspicuous yet meeting this calamity?'
translations.idiomatic: Why should clarity of mind buy a man such trouble?"

sentences.zh: ”十一年，除郎中，遷谏議大夫。

translations.literal: ' In the eleventh year he was appointed Gentleman of the Palace and promoted to Grandee Remonstrant and Consultant.
translations.idiomatic: In 68 CE he became a gentleman of the palace, then grandee remonstrant.

sentences.zh: 卒于家。

translations.literal: He died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home.

sentences.zh: 周防字伟公，汝南汝陽人也。

translations.literal: Zhou Fang, courtesy name Weigong, was a man of Ruyang in Runan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Fang, Weigong, was a native of Ruyang in Runan.

sentences.zh: 父揚，少孤微，常修逆旅，以供過客，而不受其报。

translations.literal: His father Yang, in youth orphaned and lowly, constantly maintained an inn to supply passing travelers, yet did not accept their repayment.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yang, orphaned and poor, kept an inn for travelers and refused payment for the lodging.

sentences.zh: 防年十六，仕郡小吏。

translations.literal: Fang at age sixteen served as a petty clerk in the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen Zhou Fang was a commandery clerk.

sentences.zh: 世祖巡狩汝南，召掾史试經，防尤能誦讀，拜爲守丞。

translations.literal: Shizu toured and hunted in Runan, summoned clerks and tested them on the classics; Fang was especially able to recite and read, and was appointed assistant magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Guangwu inspected Runan he examined the staff on the canons; Zhou Fang topped the trial recitation and was named assistant magistrate.

sentences.zh: 防以未冠，谒去。

translations.literal: Fang, because he had not yet capped, submitted a petition and departed.
translations.idiomatic: He declined the post because he was still under twenty.

sentences.zh: 师事徐州剌史盖豫，受《古文尚書》。

translations.literal: He took as teacher Regional Inspector Gai Yu of Xu province and received the Documents in ancient script.
translations.idiomatic: He studied the archaic-text Documents under Regional Inspector Gai Yu of Xu.

sentences.zh: 經明，舉孝廉，拜郎中。

translations.literal: When his classics were clear, he was recommended as Filial and Incorrupt and appointed Gentleman of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Once his mastery was certified he took a Filial-and-Incorrupt nomination and a gentleman's appointment.

sentences.zh: 撰《尚書杂記》三十二篇，四十萬言。

translations.literal: He composed 'Miscellaneous Records on the Documents' in thirty-two chapters, four hundred thousand graphs.
translations.idiomatic: He produced thirty-two fascicles of miscellaneous notes on the Documents—some four hundred thousand characters.

sentences.zh: 太尉張禹荐补博士，稍遷陳留太守，坐法免。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Zhang Yu recommended him to fill an Erudite post; he was gradually promoted to Administrator of Chenliu, then dismissed on account of violating the law.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Zhang Yu nominated him for the academy; he rose to governor of Chenliu until a legal offense ended his career.

sentences.zh: 年七十八，卒于家。

translations.literal: At age seventy-eight he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home at seventy-eight.

sentences.zh: 子舉，自有傳。

translations.literal: His son Ju has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhou Ju has a separate biography in this history.

sentences.zh: 孔僖字仲和，鲁國鲁人也。

translations.literal: Kong Xi, courtesy name Zhonghe, was a man of Lu in the state of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Xi, Zhonghe, came from the ducal seat of Lu.

sentences.zh: 自安國以下，世傳《古文尚書》、《毛詩》。

translations.literal: From Anguo downward, for generations the family transmitted the Documents in ancient script and the Mao Odes.
translations.idiomatic: Since Kong Anguo's day the house had taught the archaic Documents and the Mao Odes.

sentences.zh: 曾祖父子建，少游長安，与崔篆友善。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather's son Zijian, in youth roamed Chang'an and was friendly with Cui Zhuan.
translations.idiomatic: His collateral ancestor Zijian studied in Chang'an and befriended Cui Zhuan.

sentences.zh: 及篆仕王莽爲建新大尹，尝勸子建仕。

translations.literal: When Zhuan took office under Wang Mang as grand intendant of Jianxin, he once urged Zijian to take office.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Zhuan became Wang Mang's grand intendant of Jianxin, he tried to coax Zijian into government service.

sentences.zh: 對曰：“吾有布衣之心，子有衮冕之志，各从所好，不亦善乎！

translations.literal: He replied, saying: 'I have the mind of a plain-clothed commoner; you have the ambition of court robes and caps—let each follow what he loves—is it not good!'
translations.idiomatic: Zijian replied, "You crave the court; I am content in coarse cloth—let each follow his own bent."

sentences.zh: 道既乘矣，请从此辞。

translations.literal: The Way is already divergent; I beg from this to take leave.'
translations.idiomatic: Our paths have forked—let us part here."

sentences.zh: ”遂歸，終于家。

translations.literal: ' Thereupon he returned and ended his life at home.
translations.idiomatic: He went home and never took office again.

sentences.zh: 僖与崔篆孫駰复相友善，同游太學，习《春秋》。

translations.literal: Xi and Cui Zhuan's grandson Yin were again mutually friendly; together they studied at the Imperial Academy and studied the Spring and Autumn.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Xi and Cui Yin, Zhuan's grandson, became friends at the Imperial Academy over the Spring and Autumn.

sentences.zh: 因讀吴王夫差時事，僖廢書叹曰：“若是，所謂画龍不成反爲狗者。

translations.literal: Because they read the affairs of the time of King Fuchai of Wu, Xi cast aside the book and sighed, saying: 'If it is like this, it is what is called failing to finish painting a dragon and instead making a dog.'
translations.idiomatic: Reading of King Fuchai of Wu, Kong Xi slammed the book shut and said, "So much for painting a dragon—you only end up with a dog."

sentences.zh: ”駰曰：“然。

translations.literal: ' Yin said: 'It is so.'
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yin agreed.

sentences.zh: 昔孝武皇帝始爲天子，年方十八，崇信聖道，师則先王，五六年间，号胜文、景。

translations.literal: ' Formerly Emperor Xiaowu, when he first became Son of Heaven, was only eighteen years old; he honored and trusted the sages' Way, took the former kings as teachers, and within five or six years was styled superior to Wen and Jing.'
translations.idiomatic: "Emperor Wu began at eighteen," said Cui, "revering the classics and modeling himself on the ancient kings—within a few years people said he had outshone Emperors Wen and Jing."

sentences.zh: 及后恣己，忘其前之爲善。

translations.literal: When afterward he indulged himself, he forgot his former doing of good.'
translations.idiomatic: Then he indulged every whim and forgot the good ruler he had been."

sentences.zh: ”僖曰：“書傳若此多矣！

translations.literal: ' Xi said: 'In documents and transmissions it is like this in many cases!'
translations.idiomatic: Kong Xi said, "The histories are full of such turns."

sentences.zh: ”邻房生梁郁□和之曰：“如此，武帝亦是狗邪？

translations.literal: ' The neighboring-room student Liang Yu (text damaged) harmonized with it, saying: 'If it is thus, was Emperor Wu also a dog?'
translations.idiomatic: A student in the next cell, Liang Yu, chimed in: "By that logic, was Emperor Wu a dog too?"

sentences.zh: ”僖、駰默然不對。

translations.literal: ' Xi and Yin were silent and did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Xi and Cui Yin said nothing.

sentences.zh: 郁怒恨之，陰上書告駰、僖誹谤先帝，刺讥当世。

translations.literal: Yu was angry and resented them; secretly he submitted a memorial accusing Yin and Xi of slandering former emperors and satirizing the present age.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Yu, furious, filed a secret denunciation accusing them of defaming past emperors and mocking the reign.

sentences.zh: 事下有司，駰诣吏受讯。

translations.literal: The matter was sent down to the responsible offices; Yin went to the clerks and received interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: The case went to the judiciary; Cui Yin surrendered for questioning.

sentences.zh: 僖以吏捕方至，恐誅，乃上書肃宗自訟曰：

translations.literal: Xi, because the arresting clerks were about to arrive, feared execution, and thereupon submitted a memorial to Emperor Suzong suing in his own behalf, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Kong Xi, hearing that the bailiffs were on their way, feared execution and rushed a memorial to Emperor Zhang in his own defense. It read:

sentences.zh: 帝始亦无罪僖等意，及書奏，立詔勿問，拜僖兰台令史。

translations.literal: The emperor at first also had no intention of finding Xi and the others guilty; when the memorial was submitted, he immediately issued an edict not to pursue the matter, and appointed Xi Orchid Terrace clerk.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had meant no harm; when the memorial arrived he dropped the case at once and named Kong Xi a clerk of the Orchid Terrace.

sentences.zh: 元和二年春，帝東巡狩，還過鲁，幸阙里，以太牢祠孔子及七十二弟子，作六代之乐，大会孔氏男子二十以上者六十三人，命儒者講《論语》。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year of Yuanhe, the emperor toured east on the hunt; returning he passed through Lu, favored Que Village, and with the grand sacrifice sacrificed to Confucius and the seventy-two disciples; he performed the music of the six dynasties, greatly assembled sixty-three males of the Kong clan aged twenty and above, and ordered Confucians to lecture on the Analects.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 85 CE, returning from an eastern tour, the emperor stopped at Qufu, offered the great sacrifice to Confucius and the seventy-two disciples, staged the ancient six-dynasty dances, gathered sixty-three Kong clansmen over twenty, and had scholars lecture on the Analects.

sentences.zh: 僖因自陳谢。

translations.literal: Xi thereupon personally set forth thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Xi came forward to give thanks.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：“今日之会，宁于卿宗有光荣乎？

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'Does today's assembly perhaps bring glory to your clan?'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "Does today's gathering bring honor to your house?"

sentences.zh: ”對曰：“臣聞明王聖主，莫不尊师贵道。

translations.literal: ' He replied, saying: 'Your servant has heard that enlightened kings and sage lords, none fail to honor teachers and esteem the Way.'
translations.idiomatic: Kong Xi answered, "Every worthy ruler honors teachers and exalts learning."

sentences.zh: 今陛下親屈萬乘，辱臨敝里，此乃崇禮先师，增辉聖德。

translations.literal: ' Now Your Majesty personally humbles the myriad chariots and condescends to visit this mean village—this is exalting ritual toward the former teacher and adding luster to sage virtue.'
translations.idiomatic: That Your Majesty should humble the imperial chariot and visit our humble town exalts the First Teacher and adds luster to Your own virtue."

sentences.zh: 至于光荣，非所敢承。

translations.literal: ' As for glory, it is not what I dare receive.'
translations.idiomatic: As for glory to ourselves—we dare not claim it."

sentences.zh: ”帝大笑曰：“非聖者子孫，焉有斯言乎！

translations.literal: ' The emperor laughed greatly and said: 'Were he not a sage's descendant, how could there be such words!'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed aloud. "Only a descendant of the sage could speak so."

sentences.zh: ”遂拜僖郎中，賜褒成侯損及孔氏男女线、帛，詔僖从還京师，使校書東觀。

translations.literal: ' Thereupon he appointed Xi Gentleman of the Palace, granted thread and silk to Marquis of Baocheng Sun and to the males and females of the Kong clan, ordered Xi to follow in returning to the capital, and had him collate books at the Eastern Pavilion.'
translations.idiomatic: He named Kong Xi a gentleman of the court, gave silk to Marquis Sun of Baocheng and the Kong family, and ordered Kong Xi back to Luoyang to collate texts in the Eastern Pavilion library.

sentences.zh: 冬，拜臨晋令，崔駰以《家林》筮之，謂爲不吉，止僖曰：“子盍辞乎？
