translations.literal: In winter he was appointed magistrate of Linjin; Cui Yin by the 'Forest of the House' divined for him, deeming it inauspicious, and stopped Xi, saying: 'Why do you not decline?'
translations.idiomatic: That winter he was made magistrate of Linjin; Cui Yin cast the family divination text and found ill omens, and urged him to decline the post.

sentences.zh: ”僖曰：“學不爲人，仕不择官，凶吉由己，而由卜乎？

translations.literal: ' Xi said: 'Learning is not for others' sake; taking office does not mean choosing an office; fortune and misfortune lie with oneself—do they lie with divination?'
translations.idiomatic: Kong Xi replied, "One studies for truth, not for patrons; one serves where sent. Are we ruled by milfoil or by ourselves?"

sentences.zh: ”在县三年，卒官，遺令即葬。

translations.literal: ' He was in the county three years, died in office, and left instructions for immediate burial.'
translations.idiomatic: He governed three years and died in post, leaving orders to be buried on the spot.

sentences.zh: 二子：長彦、季彦，并十余歲。

translations.literal: Two sons: Changyan and Jiyan, both more than ten years old.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Changyan and Jiyan were still young boys.

sentences.zh: 蒲坂令许君然勸令反鲁。

translations.literal: The magistrate of Puban, Xu Junran, urged them to order a return to Lu.
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate of Puban, Xu Junran, urged the boys to take their father's body home to Lu.

sentences.zh: 對曰：“今載柩而歸，則违父令；

translations.literal: They replied, saying: 'Now if we load the bier and return, then we violate the father's command;'
translations.idiomatic: They answered, "To haul the coffin north would disobey our father's last words;"

sentences.zh: 舍墓而去，心所不忍。

translations.literal: 'to leave the grave site and go away is what the heart cannot bear.'
translations.idiomatic: to abandon him here would break our hearts."

sentences.zh: ”遂留华陰。

translations.literal: ' Thereupon they remained at Huayin.
translations.idiomatic: So they buried him at Huayin.

sentences.zh: 初，平帝時王莽秉政，乃封孔子后孔均爲褒成侯，追谥孔子爲褒成宣尼。

translations.literal: At first, in the time of Emperor Ping, when Wang Mang held power, he thereupon enfeoffed Kong Jun, a descendant of Confucius, as marquis of Baocheng, and posthumously gave Confucius the title Expositor Ni of Baocheng.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ping, Wang Mang had enfeoffed Kong Jun as marquis of Baocheng and posthumously titled Confucius Expositor Ni of Baocheng.

sentences.zh: 及莽敗，失國。

translations.literal: When Mang was defeated, the state was lost.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Mang fell, the marquisate lapsed.

sentences.zh: 建武十三年，世祖复封均子志爲褒成侯。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Jianwu, Shizu again enfeoffed Jun's son Zhi as marquis of Baocheng.
translations.idiomatic: In 37 CE Emperor Guangwu restored the title on Kong Jun's son Kong Zhi.

sentences.zh: 志卒，子損嗣。

translations.literal: When Zhi died, his son Sun inherited.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhi died, his son Sun succeeded.

sentences.zh: 永元四年，徙封褒亭侯。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongyuan, the enfeoffment was moved and he was enfeoffed as marquis of Baoting.
translations.idiomatic: In 92 CE the fief was moved to the marquisate of Baoting.

sentences.zh: 損卒，子曜嗣。

translations.literal: When Sun died, his son Yao inherited.
translations.idiomatic: Sun was succeeded by his son Yao.

sentences.zh: 曜卒，子完嗣。

translations.literal: When Yao died, his son Wan inherited.
translations.idiomatic: Yao was succeeded by his son Wan.

sentences.zh: 世世相傳，至献帝初，國絕。

translations.literal: Generation after generation transmitted in succession; down to the beginning of Emperor Xian, the state was cut off.
translations.idiomatic: The line continued until the early years of Emperor Xian, when the marquisate died out.

sentences.zh: 楊伦字仲理，陳留東昏人也。

translations.literal: Yang Lun, courtesy name Zhongli, was a man of Donghun in Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Lun, Zhongli, was from Donghun in Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 少爲諸生，师事司徒丁鸿，习《古文尚書》。

translations.literal: In youth he was a student; he took as teacher Grand Minister of Education Ding Hong and studied the Documents in ancient script.
translations.idiomatic: As a young scholar he studied the archaic Documents under Grand Minister of Education Ding Hong.

sentences.zh: 爲郡文學掾。

translations.literal: He became commandery clerk for letters and learning.
translations.idiomatic: He served as the commandery's education officer.

sentences.zh: 更历数将，志乘于時，以不能人间事，遂去职，不复應州郡命。

translations.literal: He passed through service under several generals; his aims rode roughshod over the times; because he could not manage human affairs in the world, he thereupon left office and no longer answered commandery and provincial orders.
translations.idiomatic: He served under a succession of generals but despised the compromises of public life, resigned, and ignored every summons from province or commandery.

sentences.zh: 講授于大澤中，弟子至千余人。

translations.literal: He lectured in a great marsh; disciples reached more than a thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: He taught in the marsh country to an audience of more than a thousand.

sentences.zh: 元初中，郡禮请，三府并辟，公車征，皆辞疾不就。

translations.literal: In the early Yuanchu period, the commandery invited him with ritual, the three offices jointly summoned him, and the imperial coach summoned him—each time he declined citing illness and did not take up office.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanchu era the commandery, the three excellencies, and the imperial coach all called for him; each time he pleaded illness.

sentences.zh: 后特征博士，爲清河王傅。

translations.literal: Later he was specially summoned as Erudite and became tutor to the king of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: He was eventually summoned to an Erudite chair and made tutor to the king of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 是歲，安帝崩，伦辄弃官奔丧，号泣阙下不絕聲。

translations.literal: That year Emperor An died; Lun thereupon cast aside office and ran to mourning, wailing beneath the palace gate without ceasing sound.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor An died that year, Yang Lun threw down his post and rushed to the capital, weeping without pause beneath the palace gate.

sentences.zh: 閻太后以其专擅去职，坐抵罪。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Yan, because he had on his own authority left office, sat him guilty to the point of punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Yan had him prosecuted for abandoning his post without leave.

sentences.zh: 陽嘉二年，征拜太中大夫。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yangjia he was summoned and appointed Grand Counsellor of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In 133 CE he was recalled as grand counsellor of the palace.

sentences.zh: 大将军梁商以爲長史。

translations.literal: Grand General Liang Shang made him chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Liang Shang named him chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 谏诤不合，出补常山王傅，病不之官。

translations.literal: His remonstrance did not accord; he went out to fill a post as tutor to the king of Changshan, but on account of illness did not go to office.
translations.idiomatic: His blunt advice offended his superiors; he was sent out as tutor to the king of Changshan but never took up the post, pleading illness.

sentences.zh: 詔書敕司隶催促发遣，伦乃留河内朝歌，以疾自上，曰：“有留死一尺，无北行一寸。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Metropolitan Commandant urgently to dispatch him; Lun thereupon stayed at Zhaoge in Henei and on account of illness reported upward, saying: 'I would rather remain dead one foot than go north one inch.'
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the metropolitan commandant to hurry him north; Yang Lun stopped at Zhaoge in Henei and sent up a memorial: "I would sooner die here than move one inch toward the north."

sentences.zh: 刎颈不易，九裂不恨。

translations.literal: Cutting the throat I will not change; nine rendings I will not regret.'
translations.idiomatic: You may cut my throat or tear me limb from limb—I will not go."

sentences.zh: 匹夫所执，强于三军。

translations.literal: What a common man holds fast is stronger than three armies.'
translations.idiomatic: A commoner's resolve can outface an army."

sentences.zh: 固敢有辞。

translations.literal: I therefore dare to have a plea.'
translations.idiomatic: That is why I dare to refuse."

sentences.zh: ”帝乃下詔曰：“伦出幽升高，宠以籓傅，稽留王命，擅止道路，托疾自从，苟肆狷志。

translations.literal: ' The emperor thereupon issued an edict saying: 'Lun came out from obscurity and ascended to high office; he was favored with a tutor post to a feudal king; he delayed royal commands, on his own authority stopped himself on the road, pleaded illness to follow his own course, and wantonly indulged a narrow will.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor answered with an edict accusing him of defying an imperial summons, blocking the highway, feigning illness, and indulging obstinacy.

sentences.zh: ”遂征诣廷尉，有詔原罪。

translations.literal: ' Thereupon he was summoned to the Commandant of Justice, and there was an edict pardoning his crime.'
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned before the commandant of justice but then pardoned.

sentences.zh: 伦前后三征，皆以直谏不合。

translations.literal: Lun, front and back three times summoned, each time because of straight remonstrance did not accord.
translations.idiomatic: Three times the court summoned him; each time his blunt counsel cost him his place.

sentences.zh: 既歸，闭门講授，自絕人事。

translations.literal: When he had returned, he closed his gate, lectured and taught, and cut himself off from human affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Back home he shut his gate, taught his students, and broke with the world.

sentences.zh: 公車复征，逊遁不行，卒于家。

translations.literal: The imperial coach summoned him again; he yielded and fled and did not go, and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Another imperial summons found him in hiding; he died at home without serving again.

sentences.zh: 中興，北海牟融习《大夏侯尚書》，東海王良习《小夏侯尚書》，沛國桓荣习《歐陽尚書》。

translations.literal: At the restoration, Mou Rong of Beihai studied the Greater Xiahou Documents, Wang Liang of the Eastern Sea studied the Lesser Xiahou Documents, and Huan Rong of Pei studied the Ouyang Documents.
translations.idiomatic: After the restoration, Mou Rong of Beihai taught the Greater Xiahou Documents, Wang Liang of Donghai the Lesser Xiahou recension, and Huan Rong of Pei the Ouyang text.

sentences.zh: 荣世习相傳授，東京最盛。

translations.literal: Rong's generations practiced mutual transmission and handing on; in the Eastern Capital it was the most flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: The Huan family transmitted the Ouyang Documents from father to son until it overshadowed every other line in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 扶風杜林傳《古文尚書》，林同郡贾逵爲之作訓，馬融作傳，鄭玄注解，由是《古文尚書》遂显于世。

translations.literal: Du Lin of Fufeng transmitted the Documents in ancient script; Jia Kui of Lin's same commandery for him made glosses, Ma Rong made a tradition, and Zheng Xuan annotated and explained—whereby the Documents in ancient script thereupon became illustrious in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Du Lin of Fufeng brought the archaic-text Documents south; Jia Kui of the same commandery glossed them, Ma Rong wrote a commentary, and Zheng Xuan annotated them—until the old-graph recension rivaled the Ouyang school in influence.
